narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 51.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above even odds, so this is a borderline statistical prediction rather than a certainty that you cannot succeed. Gender and race were not used in the prediction.

The strongest factor was your third-year class rank: you are in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That low rank pushed the prediction most strongly toward bar-exam failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 was the second most important factor; because it is above the accepted-student average of 3.23, it pushed toward passing and worked in your favor. The third most important factor was your first-year class rank: again being in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted average near the sixth decile, pushed toward failure. Together, the two very low class-rank deciles outweighed the positive signal from your GPA.

To improve a future application, focus on showing sustained academic improvement and addressing the early class-rank weakness through additional coursework, strong letters, or a clear academic plan. Consider retaking the LSAT, since your 29 is below the accepted average of 37.18, and seek admissions counseling on how to present a stronger case.
